records.literal_gloss: A song. A psalm of Asaph.

en.L: A song. A psalm of Asaph.
en.B: A song. A psalm of Asaph.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: Asaph: a leader of the temple singers
decisions.reason: Asaph was a Levite whom David appointed to lead the singing before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:5-7); his family carried on the work. Psalms 50 and 73-83 bear his name. "Of Asaph" may mean the psalm belongs to his family's collection. This is the last of them.

decisions.choice: a song, a psalm: two words for a sung poem
decisions.reason: The first word (shir) is the ordinary word for a song; the second (mizmor) a song sung to music. Several titles put them together (48:1; 66:1).

decisions.choice: a song
decisions.reason: Readable uses one word for the pair (m3).

records.literal_gloss: God, let there not be rest to you; do not be silent and do not be still, God.

en.L: God, let there be no rest for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; do not be silent and do not be still, God.
en.B: God, do not rest! Do not keep silent, and do not sit idle, God!
en.R: God, do not stay quiet! Say something! Do something, God!

decisions.choice: rest ... silent ... still: three words for doing nothing
decisions.reason: The three verbs ask God not to stay quiet or inactive while his enemies act (verse 3). The same plea is made in 28:1 and 109:1.

decisions.choice: God: 'El
decisions.reason: The verse begins with 'Elohim and ends with 'El, the shorter word for God.

decisions.choice: Say something! Do something!
alternatives: do not be silent; do not be still
decisions.reason: Readable turns the negative requests into positive ones with the same meaning.

source.text: כִּֽי־הִנֵּ֣ה א֭וֹיְבֶיךָ יֶהֱמָי֑וּן וּ֝מְשַׂנְאֶ֗יךָ נָ֣שְׂאוּ רֹֽאשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: For look, your enemies roar, and [those who] hate you have lifted up [the] head.

en.L: For look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies roar, and those who hate {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have lifted up [the] head.
en.B: Look, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} enemies are in an uproar; those who hate {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} hold their heads high.
en.R: Look! Your enemies are making a lot of noise. The people who hate {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are proud and ready to attack.

decisions.choice: roar: be in uproar
decisions.reason: The verb (hamah) is used of the roaring sea and the raging nations (46:4, 7).

decisions.choice: lifted up the head: rose up proudly
decisions.reason: To lift the head is to show pride and readiness to fight (Judges 8:28).

decisions.choice: your enemies: God's enemies
decisions.reason: The nations are against Israel (verse 4), but the psalm calls them God's enemies, for they plot against his people.

decisions.choice: proud and ready to attack
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m2).

records.literal_gloss: Against your people they make crafty counsel, and they consult together against your treasured [ones].

en.L: Against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people they make crafty plans, and they consult together against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} treasured ones.
en.B: They are plotting slyly against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people and conspiring against those {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} treasure.
en.R: They are making clever plans to hurt {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. They are plotting against the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} love and protect.

decisions.choice: your treasured ones: those God keeps safe
decisions.reason: The word (tsafun) means hidden or stored away, like a treasure. God hides his people in his shelter (27:5; 31:21).

decisions.choice: counsel: a secret plan
decisions.reason: The word (sod) is a close circle and its private plans.

source.text: אָמְר֗וּ לְ֭כוּ וְנַכְחִידֵ֣ם מִגּ֑וֹי וְלֹֽא־יִזָּכֵ֖ר שֵֽׁם־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עֽוֹד׃

records.literal_gloss: They have said, Come, and let us wipe them out from [being] a nation, and let not be remembered [the] name of Israel again.

en.L: They have said, "Come, and let us wipe them out from [being] a nation, and let the name of Israel not be remembered again."
en.B: They say, "Come, let us wipe them out so they are no longer a nation; let no one ever again remember the name of Israel."
en.R: They say, "Come on! Let us destroy Israel so it is not a nation anymore. Then no one will ever remember its name again."

decisions.choice: the name of Israel not remembered: Israel wiped out
decisions.reason: A people whose name is no longer remembered has ceased to exist. The enemies want to do to Israel what God said he would do to Amalek (Exodus 17:14), and Amalek is among them (verse 8).

decisions.choice: wipe them out: destroy completely
decisions.reason: The verb (kachad, causative) means to make something disappear.

source.text: כִּ֤י נוֹעֲצ֣וּ לֵ֣ב יַחְדָּ֑ו עָ֝לֶ֗יךָ בְּרִ֣ית יִכְרֹֽתוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: For they have consulted [with one] heart together; against you a covenant they make,

en.L: For they have consulted together [with one] heart; against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} they make a covenant,
en.B: They have agreed together with one mind; they are making a treaty against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}},
en.R: They have all agreed on a plan. They have made a treaty to fight against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: covenant: a treaty
decisions.reason: The word (berit) is used for treaties between peoples. The nations make a treaty against the God whose covenant binds him to Israel.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verses 7-8 list who makes the treaty, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.literal_gloss: [the] tents of Edom and [the] Ishmaelites, Moab and [the] Hagrites,

en.L: the tents of Edom and [the] Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
en.B: Edom's tent-dwellers, the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
en.R: Edom's people are part of it, and the Ishmaelites, the Moabites and the Hagrites.

decisions.choice: the tents of Edom: the clans of Edom
decisions.reason: "Tents" stands for the people who live in them (78:51).

decisions.choice: Israel's neighbors to the south and east
decisions.reason: Edom descended from Esau (Genesis 36:1); the Ishmaelites were desert tribes descended from Ishmael (Genesis 25:12-18); Moab descended from Lot (Genesis 19:37); the Hagrites were a people east of the Jordan (1 Chronicles 5).

decisions.choice: are part of it
decisions.reason: Readable makes the list a sentence of its own.

source.text: גְּבָ֣ל וְ֭עַמּוֹן וַעֲמָלֵ֑ק פְּ֝לֶ֗שֶׁת עִם־יֹ֥שְׁבֵי צֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, Philistia with [the] inhabitants of Tyre.

en.L: Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, Philistia with the inhabitants of Tyre.
en.B: Gebal, Ammon and Amalek, Philistia and the people who live in Tyre.
en.R: So are Gebal, Ammon and Amalek, and the Philistines, together with the people of Tyre.

decisions.choice: Gebal: a people near Edom, or the city of Byblos
alternatives: Byblos, on the coast north of Tyre
decisions.reason: The name may be a region south of the Dead Sea, near Edom, or the Phoenician port of Gebal (Byblos; Ezekiel 27:9).

decisions.choice: Ammon, Amalek, Philistia and Tyre
decisions.reason: Ammon lay east of the Jordan; Amalek was a desert people and an old enemy (Exodus 17:8-16); Philistia lay on the southern coast and Tyre on the northern. Israel is surrounded on every side. No single war in the historical books matches the whole list.

source.text: גַּם־אַ֭שּׁוּר נִלְוָ֣ה עִמָּ֑ם הָ֤י֥וּ זְר֖וֹעַ לִבְנֵי־ל֣וֹט סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Also Assyria has joined with them; they have become an arm for [the] children of Lot. Selah.

en.L: Also Assyria has joined with them; they have become an arm for the children of Lot. Selah
en.B: Assyria too has joined them; they lend their strength to the descendants of Lot. Selah
en.R: Even Assyria has joined them. They have made the descendants of Lot stronger. Selah

decisions.choice: the children of Lot: Moab and Ammon
decisions.reason: Moab and Ammon descended from Lot, Abraham's nephew (Genesis 19:36-38; Deuteronomy 2:9, 19).

decisions.choice: an arm: strength, support
decisions.reason: The arm stands for power; Assyria lends its might to the others (79:11).

decisions.choice: Assyria: the great power of the north
decisions.reason: Assyria was the empire that destroyed the northern kingdom in 722 BC. Here it is only the strongest of the allies.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: עֲשֵֽׂה־לָהֶ֥ם כְּמִדְיָ֑ן כְּֽסִֽיסְרָ֥א כְ֝יָבִ֗ין בְּנַ֣חַל קִישֽׁוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Do to them as [to] Midian, as [to] Sisera, as [to] Jabin at [the] wadi of Kishon,

en.L: Do to them as [to] Midian, as [to] Sisera, as [to] Jabin at the wadi of Kishon,
en.B: Treat them the way {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} treated Midian, the way {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} treated Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon valley,
en.R: Defeat them as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} defeated the Midianites. Defeat them as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} defeated Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon River.

decisions.choice: Midian: Gideon's victory
decisions.reason: God gave Gideon victory over the Midianites with three hundred men (Judges 7; Isaiah 9).

decisions.choice: Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon
decisions.reason: Jabin, a king of Canaan, and Sisera, his general, were defeated when the Kishon flooded and swept the army away (Judges 4:2-7; 5:21).

decisions.choice: wadi: a stream bed that floods in the rainy season
decisions.reason: The word (nachal) is a valley with a stream that runs mostly in winter.

decisions.choice: the way you treated (B); defeat them as you defeated (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what God did to these enemies.

records.literal_gloss: [who] were destroyed at Endor; they became dung for the ground.

en.L: [who] were destroyed at Endor; they became dung for the ground.
en.B: who were wiped out at Endor and became manure on the ground.
en.R: They were destroyed at Endor. Their dead bodies lay on the ground and rotted like manure.

decisions.choice: Endor: a town near the battlefield
decisions.reason: Endor lay near Mount Tabor and the Kishon (Joshua 17:11), where Sisera's army was defeated (Judges 4:14-16). Judges does not name it; the psalm may draw on another memory of the battle.

decisions.choice: dung for the ground: left to rot unburied
decisions.reason: Bodies left on the field were a mark of shame and judgment (Jeremiah 16:4).

decisions.choice: their dead bodies lay on the ground and rotted
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture (m2).

source.text: שִׁיתֵ֣מוֹ נְ֭דִיבֵמוֹ כְּעֹרֵ֣ב וְכִזְאֵ֑ב וּֽכְזֶ֥בַח וּ֝כְצַלְמֻנָּ֗ע כָּל־נְסִיכֵֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Make them, their nobles, like Oreb and like Zeeb, and like Zebah and like Zalmunna all their princes,

en.L: Make them, their nobles, like Oreb and like Zeeb, and like Zebah and like Zalmunna all their princes,
en.B: Deal with their nobles as with Oreb and Zeeb, and with all their chiefs as with Zebah and Zalmunna,
en.R: Do to their leaders what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did to Oreb and Zeeb. Do to all their rulers what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did to Zebah and Zalmunna.

decisions.choice: Oreb, Zeeb, Zebah and Zalmunna
decisions.reason: These were the leaders of Midian killed in Gideon's war (Judges 7:25; 8:21).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The princes are described in verse 13, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָ֭מְרוּ נִ֣ירֲשָׁה לָּ֑נוּ אֵ֝֗ת נְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: who said, Let us take possession for ourselves [of] the pastures of God.

en.L: who said, "Let us take possession for ourselves of the pastures of God."
en.B: who said, "Let us take God's pasturelands as our own."
en.R: They said, "Let us take for ourselves the land where God's people live."

decisions.choice: the pastures of God: the land of Israel
decisions.reason: The word (na'ot) means pastures or homesteads. The land where God's flock lives is his land (79:1, 7).

decisions.choice: who: the enemies' leaders
decisions.reason: "Who" refers back to the nobles and princes of the enemy now attacking, not to the Midianite leaders of the past.

decisions.choice: the land where God's people live
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pastures are (m1).

records.literal_gloss: My God, make them like the whirl, like chaff before [the] wind.

en.L: My God, make them like the whirling dust, like chaff before [the] wind.
en.B: My God, make them like a tumbleweed spinning away, like husks driven by the wind.
en.R: My God, blow them away like dust that spins in the wind, like the husks of grain.

decisions.choice: the whirl: whirling dust or tumbleweed
decisions.reason: The word (galgal) means a wheel or something that whirls: dust whirled by the wind, or dry plants rolled along by it (Isaiah 17:13).

decisions.choice: chaff: the light husks of grain
decisions.reason: The wind carries chaff away at threshing (1:4).

records.literal_gloss: Like fire [that] burns a forest, and like a flame [that] sets ablaze mountains,

en.L: Like fire [that] burns a forest, and like a flame [that] sets mountains ablaze,
en.B: As a fire eats through a forest, as flames set the mountainsides alight,
en.R: A fire burns up a whole forest. Flames set the hills on fire.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The comparison is completed in verse 16 ("so ..."), so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

records.literal_gloss: so you will pursue them with your tempest, and with your storm wind you will terrify them.

en.L: so pursue them with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} tempest, and terrify them with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} storm wind.
en.B: so hunt them down with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} storm and fill them with terror by {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} gale.
en.R: In the same way, chase them with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} storm. Make them afraid with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong winds.

decisions.choice: pursue ... terrify: a request
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form for future action, here used as a request, as the commands in verses 10-14 are.

decisions.choice: tempest and storm: God's weapons
decisions.reason: Storm and wind are pictured as God's weapons in battle (18:8-16; 50:3).

source.text: מַלֵּ֣א פְנֵיהֶ֣ם קָל֑וֹן וִֽיבַקְשׁ֖וּ שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Fill their faces [with] shame, that they may seek your name, YHWH.

en.L: Fill their faces [with] shame, that they may seek {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Load their faces with disgrace, so that they come seeking {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Put them to shame, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, so that they will turn to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

decisions.choice: fill their faces with shame: disgrace them openly
decisions.reason: Shame shows on the face (44:16).

decisions.choice: that they may seek your name: that they turn to God
alternatives: that they may acknowledge your name
decisions.reason: The aim of their defeat is that they turn to the LORD. Verse 19 says what they should come to know. Here the divine name appears near the end of a psalm that has said "God" until now.

decisions.choice: turn to you
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of seeking God's name (m2).

records.literal_gloss: Let them be ashamed and be dismayed until forever, and let them be disgraced and perish,

en.L: Let them be ashamed and dismayed forever, and let them be disgraced and perish,
en.B: May they be shamed and terrified for all time; may they be disgraced and come to ruin,
en.R: Let them always feel ashamed and afraid. Let them be disgraced and destroyed.

decisions.choice: perish: come to ruin
decisions.reason: The verb ('avad) means to be lost or destroyed (1:6).

decisions.choice: shame and ruin, and knowledge of God
decisions.reason: The prayer for their ruin stands beside the hope that they will seek God (verse 17) and know him (verse 19). Defeat is to bring them to the truth about who God is.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The aim follows in verse 19, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: וְֽיֵדְע֗וּ כִּֽי־אַתָּ֬ה שִׁמְךָ֣ יְהוָ֣ה לְבַדֶּ֑ךָ עֶ֝לְי֗וֹן עַל־כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: and let them know that you, your name [is] YHWH, you alone, [are] Most High over all the earth.

en.L: and let them know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} alone [are] the Most High over all the earth.
en.B: and let them come to know that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, that only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are Most High over the whole earth.
en.R: Let them learn that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name is {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Let them learn that only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the God who is over all, ruling the whole earth.

decisions.choice: you, your name is the LORD, you alone
alternatives: that you alone, whose name is the LORD, are the Most High
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is broken up for emphasis: "you" is said, then the name is given, then "you alone". The sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: Most High: God above all
decisions.reason: The title ('Elyon) names God as the highest over all (Genesis 14:19; 7:18), over the nations and their gods.

decisions.choice: let them know: the nations brought to know God
decisions.reason: The goal of judgment in the prophets is that the nations "know that I am the LORD" (Ezekiel 36:23; Exodus 14:4).

decisions.choice: the God who is over all
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title means (m2).
